messages.author: a3527f6489543e9b
messages.subject: Question about 'rmc.desiredtz' from Config file
parts:
Hi Vincent and GGIR users,

I was just wondering if anyone could provide me an answer for the following question:
I just did some analysis with the accelerometry data collected using Axivity AX3. It went well until I had a look into the config file and found this variable "rmc.desiredtz" which showed a different timezone that it should have been. I looked up for the definition of this variable in the manual and it says "Timezone in which device was configured and expriments took place. If experiments took place in a different timezone, then use this argument for the timezone in whcih the experiments took place and argument configtz to specify where the device was configured (not implemented yet)".
Based on this definition the output from Config seems to tell me that the device was configured for data collection in 'Europe/London'. Is that correct? But the device should have been configured in a different time zone 'Pacific/Marshall Island'? I am not involved in the data collection so can't tell anything about it.

ps. In my analysis I set 'desiredtz' as 'Pacific/Majuro' for the analysis as that's where the device was configured and collected the data and I am based in Australia.

messages.author: 494dad402cbbbe7c
messages.subject: Re: Question about 'rmc.desiredtz' from Config file
parts:
Hi John,

I understand that one can set the desiredtz based on http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zone.tab.

For example, if you are based in NSW, Australia, then the desiredtz="Australia/NSW".

Try that, and correct me if I am wrong. Thank you

messages.author: 13568954e9b4ef4b
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Question about 'rmc.desiredtz' from Config file
parts:
rmc.desoredtz is only used when you work with custom csv format as explained in the documentation. So, I do not expect it to affect you AX3 cwa (?) analysis.
I will change the arguments default setting to local timezone rather than London to avoid confusion moving forward.

Vincent
